problem: Supervised VLN agents (BEVBert, GridMM, ScaleVLN) need dataset-specific fine-tuning and fail on out-of-domain instruction styles (e.g. REVERIE, SOON). Pure LLM agents (NavGPT, MapGPT) generalize but are weak at low-level execution, cannot distinguish nodes in the same orientation, deviate around obstacles, and are costly because they call the LLM at every step.
motivation: A deployable agent should be trained once and then follow diverse instruction types (high-level, dialog) without retraining. LLMs are good at planning and commonsense reasoning, while domain-trained models are better at executing fine-grained navigation, so a hierarchical split can combine both strengths.
key_idea: An LLM Planner turns out-of-domain instructions into fine-grained R2R-style guidances, which an ensembled R2R-trained Instruction Follower executes, with MLLM feasibility verification and LLM arbitration when the ensemble disagrees.
insight: Delegating only high-level planning to the LLM and low-level control to a supervised follower gives large zero-shot gains over both parts alone: the follower alone gets SR 31.95 with the ensemble, whereas FlexVLN reaches 39.80 on REVERIE. Ablations on a 100-episode set show that feasibility verification (SR 37 vs 34), constraining guidance to an R2R-derived action space (37 vs 30), InternVL panoramic perception with position inference (37 vs 28 for NavGPT-style BLIP-2 perception) and the topological memory map for the follower (SR 30→37) each contribute. Planning at guidance granularity also cuts LLM calls to 48% and cost to about 14% of NavGPT.
method: Environmental Perception: four 90° views per node are described by InternVL-40B in two rounds (holistic scene description, then inferred current position), plus Faster R-CNN objects within 3 m using depth, and height/floor, all rendered as text.

LLM Planning: GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini with a six-part system prompt (role, objective, inputs, outputs, abilities, constraints) reasons over the instruction, navigation history and observation, outputs a direction and a fine-grained guidance restricted to an R2R-derived action space (go forward, turn left/right, go through, go into, stop, etc.), and outputs 'Finished!' when done.

Feasibility Verification: Qwen2-VL-7B checks the guidance against the view in the chosen direction. If it is infeasible (e.g. a closed door), the reason is fed back to the planner to regenerate the guidance.

Guidance Execution (multi-model integration): BEVBert, GridMM and ScaleVLN, all trained on R2R, vote on each action. If they agree the action is executed; otherwise GPT-4o-mini picks among the textualized candidate actions given the guidance. Concatenated guidances and the topological memory map are kept.

Navigation history: the follower's trajectory is converted to text ('{direction} to {object}, facing toward {scene}') and appended for the planner. The planner is called only after each guidance completes (max 10 planner calls, max 5 follower moves per guidance).
Object Localization: GPT-4o-mini extracts the target object from the instruction, and BLIP-2 picks the object at the final node with the highest similarity to it.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini (planner, frozen) + InternVL-40B + Qwen2-VL-7B + BLIP-2 + Faster R-CNN + R2R-trained BEVBert/GridMM/ScaleVLN ensemble
setting.training_data: No training on target datasets; the Instruction Follower models are trained on R2R (ScaleVLN with its augmented data); the rest are off-the-shelf.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (4 views x 90° per node) + depth + height/position from the simulator
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (follower); planner emits text guidances from a fixed phrase set
setting.privileged: none (uses simulator height, depth and object annotations/bboxes at nodes, as in REVERIE/SOON)

numbers.extra: no REVERIE training; Instruction Follower trained on R2R

results: Zero-shot on REVERIE val-unseen, FlexVLN with GPT-4o gets SR 39.80 / SPL 29.74, beating MapGPT (GPT-4V, SR 31.6 on a 500-sample subset) and the follower ensemble (SR 31.95); it is comparable to some in-domain methods such as LANA (SR 34.00). On SOON it is the first LLM-based method, with SR 23.08 vs 3–4.6 for the R2R-trained followers. On CVDN-target it reaches GP 3.63, above HAMT (2.74) and comparable to DUET (3.70).
limitations: Still trails the best in-domain supervised models (e.g. ScaleVLN SR 56.97 on REVERIE, AutoVLN SR 41.00 on SOON), and CVDN-target was evaluated only with GPT-4o-mini.
Text-only perception loses visual information and causes planner errors (23% of sampled failures); 40% of failures come from the Instruction Follower, e.g. failing to stop or going upstairs.
Relies on the simulator's depth, height and object annotations, on a hand-defined R2R action-phrase set, and on an ensemble of three models plus several large foundation models, which is heavy.
